title: MLA Teresa Wat leaves B.C. Conservatives, the 4th departure this month
summary: MLA Teresa Wat, who represents the Richmond-Bridgeport riding, says she "can no longer serve" in the B.C. Conservative Party under its new leader Kerry-Lynne Findlay.

title: Why CBSA changes at 1 B.C. border have increased hurdles for some businesses
summary: Some Abbotsford businesses say they are continuing to face more expensive and inconvenient operations due to changes at the the Abbotsford-Huntingdon border crossing. title: Search for B.C.'s best roadside attraction: Semifinal 2, Enchanted Forest vs. Barkerville
summary: After four weeks of voting, we're left with Cathedral Grove as one of the two finalists in the Search for B.C.'s Best Roadside Attraction. But what will it face?

title: What's at stake in the North Vancouver federal byelection?
summary: Voters head to the polls Aug. 31 in one of three federal byelections, with the federal Liberals one seat short of a majority government.

title: New hatcheries will see up to 1 million more salmon raised and released into Fraser and Skeena Rivers annually
summary: "Salmon are not simply a resource," Lheidli T'enneh Chief Dolleen Logan said at the announcement held in Prince George Tuesday. "Salmon are relatives. They are a part of our culture, our identity, our laws, our responsibilities."

title: FOI reveals operator of Sandman Hotel chain fined over $620K for asbestos violations
summary: In the report — which details the $624,051.48 penalty handed to Northland Properties — B.C.'s workplace regulator says the company failed to ensure workers were safe when they worked on a renovation project at the Williams Lake hotel in December 2025.

title: B.C. premier urges feds to reconsider fighter jet purchase, coal shipments as U.S. trade war ramps up
summary: B.C. Premier David Eby said that the province was supportive of Canadian counter-tariffs as the trade war with the U.S. ramps up — but urged the federal government to consider non-tariff measures to hit back at punishing U.S. duties.

title: Advocate worries crisis is being forgotten as B.C. toxic drug deaths tick up in June
summary: The B.C. Coroners Service said it recorded 138 suspected toxic drug deaths across the province in June — representing an increase from the previous month, but a decrease from the same month last year.

title: Rosalyn Bird is latest MLA to leave Kerry-Lynne Findlay's B.C. Conservatives
summary: Rosalyn Bird, the MLA for Prince George-Valemount, is the latest MLA to leave the B.C. Conservative caucus. It comes on the heels of the departures of Ian Paton and Peter Milobar, who say they plan to set up a new political party.

title: Unionized Metro Vancouver workers to continue some job action as parties agree to binding arbitration
summary: Unionized outside workers have been staging job action over the last few months with pickets going up at regional parks, water treatment facilities and Metro Vancouver headquarters, among other places.

title: Search for B.C.'s best roadside attraction: Semifinal 1, Othello Tunnels vs. Cathedral Grove
summary: The story of British Columbia's complex relationship with our natural environment, our early attempts to control it, and our later attempts to celebrate it can be seen in the places voters have chosen to reach the final four of Search for B.C.'s Roadside Attraction.

title: Dolly Parton's 'Jolene' may be named after British Columbia nurse
summary: A Prince George woman believes she may be the inspiration for the name in Dolly Parton's song Jolene. Juline Whelan met the singer in 1972 and matches the description of the little girl Parton says inspired the name behind the famous tune.
